storyline.latest_title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models", so most of it is a reading list, not one thread. Oct 16-28 items cover sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, steering and continual learning, and Mistral Large 4 shipped Oct 29.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Nov 2: Anthropic reported progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference, and InfoQ argued agentic architectures need a context engine that selects, injects, compresses and expires information.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Mistral Large 4 is the one deployable item: vLLM support landed with the weights. The newest items point at architecture choices: how agents manage context and memory, and how inference might be verified.
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you self-host, pull Mistral Large 4 on the vLLM day-0 build and rerun your own evals before swapping it in. For agents, audit where context is selected, compressed and expired in your harness before adding more memory.

beats.headline: Hallucinations in cross-language code translation, with mitigations
Search-state awareness for RAG agents, and LLM materials-data extraction
Spectral interventions, KG-to-text benchmarking and Bashkir adaptation
Long-horizon search evals, steering, vulnerability screening, sequential feedback and memory replay
Translated-benchmark validity and RL for self-learning
beats.summary: Two papers: whether translated MMLU-style benchmarks measure language or locality, and RL that couples knowledge acquisition with reasoning.

beats.headline: Mistral Large 4 ships with day-0 vLLM and Hugging Face support
beats.summary: A concrete model release, preceded by an Oct 22 pricing comparison naming it.

beats.headline: Memory graphs, knowledge integration, retrieval compilation, parametric memory, Text-to-SQL survey and extreme pruning
beats.summary: Six papers on persistent memory, context-vs-memory evaluation, compiled knowledge for search harnesses, distilling retrieval into weights, Text-to-SQL architectures, and pruning at extreme sparsity.

beats.headline: Provable inference from Anthropic; InfoQ lays out a context engine for agents
beats.summary: Nov 2: a cryptographic-proof research update and a practitioner architecture article.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm Mistral Large 4's quality against DeepSeek and Cohere models?
Does the "9x price gap" comparison hold against first-party Mistral API pricing?
Does Reva's real-time screening keep false positives low enough to gate agent-written code?
Does CAMR's replay selection reduce forgetting on models larger than those in its experiments?
Does Anthropic's zkSNARK work reach proving times practical for production-size models?
Do the Oct 30 retrieval-compilation and parametric-memory results hold outside their reported benchmarks?
